items.body:
## Canonical owner defect

`ContextualWisdomLab/contextual-orchestrator` is the owner of model-provider discovery, credentials, capability routing/fallback, gateway behavior, and Agent timeout semantics. A current consumer repair in `ContextualWisdomLab/keyverse#132` (exact head `742ed3dddd8ff85e3caa983753f87a01a24fcc87`) cannot satisfy that boundary using a released owner interface today, so it clones this repository at commit `045d17da5e2aea56a97e241ee158ab1628d78660`, executes `scripts/ci/serve_seeded_gateway.py` from sibling source, injects five provider credentials into the Keyverse workflow, expands Keyverse egress to provider hosts, and wraps the model call with a fixed 2100-second shell timeout.

That consumer delta fixes an older direct-NVIDIA hard-coded model path, but exact-SHA source vendoring is still cross-repository implementation consumption rather than `owner RED -> GREEN -> immutable release -> consumer bump`. A model-backed GitHub Actions leaf must expose only the contextual-orchestrator gateway token plus `orchestrator/free`; provider credentials/discovery/routing/fallback remain here. Default Agent/Gateway model timeout remains null: user cancel, provider termination, and explicit audited admin timeout are separate outcomes.

The Keyverse PR also has a current-head runtime finding: its pinned launch path supplies `--auth-token-key CONTEXTUAL_ORCHESTRATOR_TOKEN`, while `serve_seeded_gateway.py` seeds provider credentials; consumer text tests do not prove authenticated gateway startup.

## Additional live consumer evidence — TEPP #480

`ContextualWisdomLab/TEPP#480` has now removed its repository-local provider discovery/ranking bootstrap and, at exact head `484c5092034430089d519468f4b95578a3a7806c`, requires an immutable contextual-orchestrator GitHub release, HTTPS gateway URL, gateway credential, and `orchestrator/free`. That is the correct consumer ownership direction, but fresh review exposed two owner-contract requirements that TEPP cannot truthfully manufacture:

- the consumer can validate a GitHub release record and independently observe `orchestrator/free` at the configured gateway, but the gateway exposes no authenticated release/provenance identity that proves the deployed API is the exact configured release/schema/artifact;
- the Actions caller must authenticate OpenCode to the gateway, but handing a reusable bearer secret to a model-controlled process leaves the credential readable/reusable by local shell execution unless the released owner contract provides a safer scoped/ephemeral credential or equivalent brokered authentication boundary.

TEPP also has a separate consumer-side redirect-hardening finding on its authenticated catalog probe; that belongs in TEPP and does not relax this owner requirement. Until this owner contract exists, TEPP #480 is intentionally non-deployable rather than falling back to mutable source or provider credentials.

Fresh owner state observed for this handoff is protected `main@e37ca8227be102dbf6059bbc2aa947f877876bfe`, advanced normally by merged #1149 on top of prior protected `96674b240ad500900849bbb093093ce969693dbc`, with zero GitHub releases. #1149 is a bounded streaming-test socket-lifecycle repair and does not create or weaken the Actions-facing gateway/release/authentication contract required here. This observation is point-in-time evidence only; implementation must re-read live state.

## Required RED

1. Add an owner integration/package test that exercises the exact released Actions-facing entrypoint as a consumer would, with only the documented gateway bootstrap interface, and proves authenticated `/v1/models` plus an `orchestrator/free` request can reach owner routing while provider credentials stay inside contextual-orchestrator ownership.
2. Add release-contract tests proving a consumer does **not** need to clone this repository, import `scripts/ci/*`, receive provider secrets, name provider hosts/models/groups, or implement fallback logic.
3. Prove missing required capability/available free route fails closed without paid/provider-specific bypass.
4. Prove the default model-call timeout is null and that provider termination, user cancellation, and explicit admin timeout remain distinguishable; no owner default may terminate reasoning/streaming/tool calls solely by elapsed wall clock.
5. Bind API/schema/client/runtime behavior to one immutable source/artifact identity and reject stale/predecessor or declaration-only evidence. The released gateway must expose authenticated metadata or an equivalent receipt whose exact release tag/version, contract/schema identity, and artifact/source digest can be compared with the immutable release provenance; a valid release record paired with a different or identity-less deployment must fail closed.
6. Add an Actions-consumer authentication regression proving the LLM-controlled process cannot read/reuse a long-lived gateway bearer credential through arbitrary local shell/tool execution. The chosen owner design may use narrowly scoped short-lived credentials, a broker/socket boundary, workload identity, or another auditable mechanism, but it must not push provider credentials or routing authority back into consumers.

## Required GREEN

Publish a minimal independently consumable versioned interface for GitHub Actions clients: released package/container/client/API schema as appropriate, exact immutable version/digest, authentication contract, `orchestrator/free` virtual-model contract, health/readiness behavior, authenticated deployment-identity/provenance evidence, error/abstention semantics, SBOM/provenance and exact-source identity. Provider credentials/discovery/egress stay entirely behind this owner boundary. If the runtime is delivered as a container/artifact, publish and verify it by immutable digest rather than asking consumers to clone source. If a central hosted gateway is the intended deployment, publish the versioned client/schema, gateway-token/identity contract, and an authenticated way for consumers to prove the running gateway corresponds to that released contract.

After exact-head owner CI/security/coverage/public-doc/package/SBOM/provenance is terminal GREEN and an immutable release exists, repair consumers by exact release/version/digest bump through thin callers. `ContextualWisdomLab/keyverse#132` and `ContextualWisdomLab/TEPP#480` should remain alive but Draft/blocked-equivalent until they can consume that released owner boundary; do not close/discard their valid removal of repository-local provider routing.

Any temporary bridge must have an owner issue, explicit expiry, and deletion criterion and must not become a second provider-routing authority.

items.body:
# KF-RD-GENAI-STACK-2026-001

## Purpose
Durable research ledger for the methodical dissection of the 2026 GenAI stack and adjacent systems, followed by scientific/work-domain parallelisation and whole-system convergence into KEYFLOWOS / KEY.

This is **research and architectural memory**, not implementation authority. Production code remains untouched until findings are converged, dependency-ordered, and separately authorized for implementation.

## Required method for every subject
1. Technical dissection: architecture, primitives, algorithms, APIs, state, persistence, execution lifecycle, concurrency, failure/retry/cancellation, security, tenancy, observability, evaluation, scaling, latency, cost, DX, extensibility, licensing, known failure modes.
2. Source inspection where code is open.
3. Microscopic comparison against live KEYFLOWOS.
4. Scientific parallelisation: neuroscience, physiology, cybernetics/control theory, information theory, graph theory, distributed systems, statistics, OR, ecology/evolution, safety engineering, etc., but only where the mechanism is structurally transferable.
5. Work/operational parallelisation: medicine, aviation, finance/accounting, logistics, industrial safety, incident response, organizations, command-and-control, etc.
6. Mechanism extraction.
7. KEY/KEYFLOWOS hypothesis.
8. Experiment + measurable proof obligation.
9. Disposition: ADOPT / ADAPT / ABSORB / MERGE / REPLACE / REMOVE / BENCHMARK / WATCH / REJECT.
10. Hold findings for convergence; do not cargo-cult dependencies.

## Dual targets
Every useful finding is assessed for:
- KEY / KEYFLOWOS runtime.
- The autonomous development machinery building KEYFLOWOS (Claude Code / control plane / repo intelligence / review loops).

## Completion standard
The programme is not complete until individual subjects are researched, cross-domain mechanisms extracted, contradictions/duplicates identified, uncertain claims experimentally resolved, and the results converged into a small set of canonical architectural primitives with explicit invariants and proof obligations.

## Inventory
Layer 1: OpenAI/GPT; Anthropic/Claude; Gemini; Llama; DeepSeek; Qwen.
Layer 2: vLLM; Ollama; llama.cpp; Groq; Bedrock; Vertex AI.
Layer 3: LangChain; LangGraph; LlamaIndex; CrewAI; AutoGen; Pydantic AI.
Layer 4: OpenAI embeddings; Cohere; Voyage; Jina; BGE; Nomic.
Layer 5: Pinecone; Qdrant; Weaviate; Milvus; Chroma; pgvector.
Layer 6: Hugging Face; PEFT/LoRA; Unsloth; Axolotl; TRL; LLaMA-Factory.
Layer 7: DSPy; Instructor; Outlines; Guidance; BAML; provider structured outputs.
Layer 8: MCP; native function calling; A2A; computer/browser use; Composio; Arcade.
Layer 9: LangSmith; Langfuse; Ragas; DeepEval; Phoenix; W&B Weave.
Layer 10: NeMo Guardrails; Guardrails AI; Llama Guard; Lakera; Presidio; Rebuff.

The inventory expands when adjacent/superior systems are discovered.

## Progress
- R&D-01A OpenAI/GPT: first-pass technical dissection completed; findings held for Layer-1 convergence.
- R&D-01B Anthropic/Claude: active.

## R&D-01A — OpenAI/GPT holding findings
- Capability-based cognitive scheduling instead of model-name routing.
- Responses-style typed cognitive event streams should map underneath KEY's own lifecycle, not replace Cortex.
- Model tool selection is evidence/intent, never business-action authority.
- Machine-facing outputs should be schema-first; human presentation should not be reparsed into state.
- Hierarchical/deferred capability discovery ("capability paging") is high-value for KEY's large tool/connector surface.
- Prompt/context layout should be designed for cache locality: stable constitution -> stable business context -> semi-stable genome/session -> dynamic turn.
- Provider conversation state is ephemeral execution state, never canonical KEY memory.
- Classify AI work as realtime / interactive / background / batch / scheduled / event-triggered.
- Create a capability/lifecycle-aware model catalog.
- Current live repo gap: OpenAI path still uses Chat Completions and direct OpenAI calls exist outside the model gateway (embeddings/vision/voice/document paths); provider boundary is not yet fully converged.

## Continuity rule
Each completed subject should add a durable comment here containing:
- source-backed findings,
- current KEYFLOWOS comparison,
- science/work parallels,
- extracted mechanisms,
- candidate experiments,
- disposition,
- interactions/contradictions with earlier findings,
- implementation implications held for convergence.

At each layer boundary, publish a layer-convergence comment before proceeding to the next layer.

items.title: [warehouse][postgres] 선언된 fact를 내구 적재·snapshot 게시·조회하고 Dataset Explorer에 연결한다
items.body:
<!-- croco-growth-direction:GD17 -->
<!-- croco-declarative-data:DW02 -->
## Priority / baseline
P1 — PostgreSQL로 시작하는 선언형 warehouse의 실제 적재·게시·조회 경로.
원 등록/보완 2026-09-21~22 `trunk@7dc3a10fb4bea30b667275e316b6e79971dde6c8`; 재검토 `trunk@c57ba6e287beeea183a0f393a9a5f61a4009f78e`.

## Ownership / in-flight work
#2856은 모델/codec, #2857은 CSV/JSONL/source 변환·checkpoint 실행, #2862는 지표·공통 authorized query/result다. 이 이슈는 모델→PG 적재→검증 snapshot 게시→bounded native reader/Dataset Explorer를 소유한다. 별도 ETL 실행 원장·모델 선언·지표 engine은 만들지 않는다.
**#2872/PR #2875가 warehouse-postgres/metrics provider 분리를 진행 중이다.** 재검토 시 미병합이므로 착수 시 최신 branch/PR을 확인하고 그 package/catalog/기존 metrics integration을 재사용한다. 같은 package를 다른 PR에서 새로 만들거나 legacy metrics layout을 fact layout으로 강제 변환하지 않는다. 기존 store 이동이 본 warehouse 구현 완료도 아니다.
출발점: MetricsRepository/TimescaleMetricsStore, batch-core/ChunkExecutor(write 뒤 별도 checkpoint), admin-core public API 및 PostgreSQL native schema/transaction. Timescale 확장은 기본 경로 필수가 아니다.

## Package / contracts
warehouse-postgres는 warehouse-core/runtime의 CatalogStore/WarehouseWriter/WarehouseReader를 구현하는 provider Plugin이다. metadata/data 동일 PG가 기본이지만 pool/credential 역할은 명시한다. app 운영 schema를 소유하지 않는다.
Catalog는 model/physical binding, candidate/snapshot/publication CAS·기본 privacy suppression만 소유하고 status/progress/checkpoint는 execution-core를 참조한다.
Candidate={id,scope,modelVersion,transformHash,sourceRefs,expectedHead,fence,state}; Snapshot={id,modelVersion,segmentRefs,partitionSelection,quality,createdAt}; WriteReceipt={batchId,attempt,state:durable|indeterminate|rejected,providerRef}.
quality는 freshness/temporalCompleteness/populationCoverage/validity/reproducibility를 구분하고 query exactness는 #2862와 같은 계약으로 보존한다.

## Native storage / publication
1. 선언 컬럼/codec에서 타입이 명시된 일반 PostgreSQL 테이블·컬럼을 파생한다. 컬럼형 스토리지 엔진이나 확장을 요구하지 않는다. 모든 fact를 하나의 JSONB payload 테이블로 저장하지 않는다. 초기 정확성은 비파티션 unique부터 확보한다. 파티션을 쓰면 unique 제약의 partition-key 요구를 명시한다. DDL은 명시 migration이며 boot에 실행하지 않는다.
2. trusted scope+model semantic generation+grain tuple가 logical identity다. sourceEventId/runId/batchId가 바뀌어도 같은 사실일 수 있다. canonical typed payload 같음은 replay, 다름은 conflict다. 명시 correction 없이 공개 사실을 덮어쓰지 않는다. provenance/attempt는 identity와 별개다.
3. unpublished candidate에 적재하고 row dedupe와 batch receipt를 모두 검증한다. commit 응답 불명은 receipt lookup/reconcile 전 무조건 새 write를 하지 않는다. timeout을 저장0건으로 해석하지 않는다.
4. append는 직전 공개 snapshot+검증된 새 segment, aggregate replacement는 날짜/series partition의 완전 generation으로 새 snapshot을 만든다. expectedHead/fence와 validation을 transaction/CAS로 확인하고 head가 전진하면 재검증한다. 옛 pinned snapshot의 논리 결과는 불변이다.
5. seal/publish와 writer가 같은 candidate 상태/fence를 lock/조건부 SQL로 검사한다. stale writer가 sealed 결과를 바꾸지 못한다. reader는 SnapshotSet을 한 번 고정하고 keyset cursor 다음 페이지에 current를 다시 읽지 않는다. 만료 snapshot은 명시 unavailable다.
6. source coverage/late/gap을 보존한다. MAX(eventTime)/API 성공/execution completed는 complete 증거가 아니다. empty 정상 partition과 partial/원천 실패를 구분하고 마지막 정상 head를 지킨다.
7. parameterized filter/projection/order, 서버 scope/필드 권한·row/byte/time/concurrency/cancel을 제공한다. read/import/export/drop/publish 역할을 나누고 현재 permission/privacy epoch를 반환/cursor/cache/publish에서 재검증한다. 기본 PG retention/delete/suppression은 여기서 실제 구현한다.

## Shared reuse / physical-cost boundary
리텐션/실험/재무/SEO/RUM/퍼널은 이 native reader를 재사용하고 개별 SQL client/warehouse를 만들지 않는다. 기능별 semantic normalizer·계산은 각 기능, parser는 #2857, RegisteredQuery/권한 runner는 #2862가 소유한다. normalized 순수 계산 소비자에 PG 설치를 강제하지 않는다.
logical generation/segment가 항상 physical table이라는 뜻은 아니다. 불변성·fencing·publication 보장을 유지하는 native 구조를 사용하고 batch마다 새 table/전체 역사 복사를 강제하지 않는다. segment/physical-object 수·read/write amplification·메모리·게시 지연·cleanup을 합성 입력으로 확인하고 숨은 무제한 증식을 막는다. schema 분리는 CPU/IO 격리가 아니므로 pool/concurrency/timeout을 문서화한다.

## Dataset Explorer
같은 서비스에서 grain·컬럼 의미·source/quality·마지막 publication·실패 candidate·bounded sample을 보여준다. 실행 완료와 게시를 구분하고 UI가 별도 schema 정답을 만들지 않는다. 재게시/제거는 actor/reason/expectedRevision/idempotency/audit·서버 권한을 따른다. PII/secret를 samples/diagnostics에 무조건 출력하지 않는다.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] capture/search aggregate를 실제 PG에 설치→적재→검증/게시→reader/Explorer로 조회한다.
- [ ] 다른 batch의 동일 행은 한 사실, 상충 payload는 conflict, 다른 tenant의 같은 grain은 격리된다.
- [ ] 두 연결 writer/publisher·commit 응답 손실·seal 뒤 늦은 write·중간 실패에서 staging이 노출되거나 정상 head가 훼손되지 않는다.
- [ ] head 전진 중 pagination은 같은 snapshot이고 권한/삭제 변경·만료를 재검증한다.
- [ ] 큰 정수/decimal/date codec·privacy suppression/재적재·freshness와 coverage 구분을 검증한다.
- [ ] legacy metrics integration과 새 fact reader가 공존하고 package/SQL reader를 중복 생성하지 않는다. physical 비용·retention 한계를 설명한다.

## Dependencies / validation / completion
#2856 모델이 실제 선행이다. ETL/GSC/다른 provider 없이 validated normalized rows로 이 provider를 직접 쓸 수 있다. #2875의 package 병합/변경과 조정하고 tx-drizzle RLS helper를 쓰는 경로는 #2325의 non-owner 허용/교차 tenant 거절 회귀가 선행이다. helper를 안 쓰는 경우 실제 동등 tenant 보장을 검증한다.
최신 AGENTS.md·실제 scripts/exports/PR을 확인하고 별도 브랜치에서 작업한다. 임시 PG 다중 연결·fresh/upgrade/restart·fault injection·native schema/codec/query·실제 UI 상태/keyboard·관련 test/typecheck/build·public API/docs/catalog·`pnpm check`를 수행한다. changeset/migration·사용법을 포함해 커밋하고 브랜치/커밋·보장/비용/한계·수행/미수행 검증을 보고한다. trunk 직접 push·수동 bump·publish·운영 데이터/유료 scan/evidence 수집 금지. 새 DB/ETL engine·전체 backfill·파일 삭제 orchestration은 범위 밖이다.

items.title: Investigate GitHub Copilot usage-metrics REST API for cost-centre spend + model-choice analysis
items.body:
## Context

GitHub Enterprise Cloud exposes [REST API endpoints for Copilot usage metrics](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/rest/copilot/copilot-usage-metrics?apiVersion=2026-03-10). Cost Compass currently only *simulates* AI-credit and budget behavior (`src/engine.js`, `scenarios/`). To follow up on real cost-centre usage we need to ingest this real data and answer two questions per cost centre/user:

1. **How much** are they spending (AI credits / paid overage)?
2. **How** are they spending it — e.g. are expensive models (higher premium-request multipliers) being used for trivial tasks like code review, versus lighter models for equivalent work?

## Ask

- Investigate the data points exposed by the enterprise/organization/user/repo/user-teams report families and the preview `usage-records` endpoint, and identify which fields support cost-centre attribution and model-choice/task-type analysis (feature, IDE, language, and model breakdown arrays such as `totals_by_model_feature`, `totals_by_language_model`, `totals_by_feature`, `ai_credits_used`, `ai_adoption_phase`, etc.).
- Determine whether the needed data is only available at daily granularity (`*-1-day`, historical up to 1 year) or also as rolling 28-day snapshots (`*-28-day/latest`, latest window only, no historical range parameter), and what that implies for how we must durably store extracted data ourselves (idempotent per-day upserts using the `day_partition`/`etl_id` housekeeping fields, since GitHub's signed download URLs expire and the 28-day endpoint has no history).
- Note the key limitation that `ai_credits_used` is a per-user/day total **not broken down by model or feature**, so per-model spend must be *estimated* by combining per-model interaction/LOC breakdowns with GitHub's published premium-request model multipliers, not read directly.
- Research how the resulting cost-centre/user spend and model-usage data could be linked into Azure cost-controlling functionality (Azure Cost Management, tagging/allocation, and the Microsoft FinOps toolkit/FOCUS data format), given Copilot spend billed through an Azure subscription is not natively broken down per user/model on the Azure invoice.
- Produce a written investigation/design summary (data points, granularity + storage implications, and the Azure cost-management linking approach) to ground a future ingestion implementation.

## Out of scope for this issue

Building the actual ingestion pipeline, storage backend, or Azure Cost Management connector — this issue is investigation/design only. A follow-up implementation issue should be filed once the approach is agreed.

items.title: feat(rocketmq): 工业级全场景加固、SimpleConsumer 租约流式拉取、定时消息精准撤回、死信受控重放与运行期运维治理
items.body:
## Problem Statement

When building high-reliability financial transaction messaging, distributed 2PC event choreography, and high-throughput microservices with Spring Boot 3 and Apache RocketMQ 5.x, developers face notable capability voids, architectural asymmetries, and operational blindspots in `ateng-boot-rocketmq`:

1. **Unidirectional Dead Letter Accumulation & Missing Governance Facade ("只死不救")**:
   RocketMQ 5.x automatically routes messages exceeding max delivery attempts (default 16) to dead letter queues (`%DLQ%<ConsumerGroup>`). While `ateng-boot-rocketmq` provides poison-pill detection to discard fatal malformed messages, it completely lacks a symmetrical management facade to safely inspect (`peek`) or programmatically replay (`replay`) dead letters back into business topics once downstream bugs are fixed. Developers are forced to manually craft ad-hoc consumers or use external tools, risking secondary dead letter avalanches and infinite crash loops without replay count tracking.
2. **Push-Only Limitations for Heavy & Long-Running Batch Workloads**:
   The starter currently only supports event-driven `@RocketmqListener` driven by `PushConsumer`. In scenarios involving micro-batch peak shaving, long-polling extraction, or long-running heavy tasks (e.g., executing for 30–60+ seconds), Push models easily cause thread-pool starvation and cannot dynamically renew the message invisibility duration (`changeInvisibleDuration`), resulting in messages prematurely reappearing and being concurrently processed by other instances.
3. **Inability to Recall Pre-Scheduled & Delayed Messages**:
   In delayed timeout scenarios such as order cancellation (e.g., auto-cancel after 30 minutes if unpaid), if the user completes payment at minute 5, the delayed message still lands at minute 30, triggering redundant database queries and state machine checks. RocketMQ 5.x natively supports message recall via `recallHandle`, but `RocketmqTemplate` currently exposes no API for this capability.
4. **Missing Batch & Oneway Send Facades**:
   `RocketmqTemplate` only exposes single-message transmission. In reconciliation synchronization or bulk notification scenarios, developers must write manual loops without unified concurrency aggregation or payload boundaries. Furthermore, high-throughput non-critical paths (e.g., audit logging, metrics pinging) lack non-blocking `sendOneway` support.
5. **Lack of Runtime Consumer Flow Control (Pause/Resume)**:
   During downstream system maintenance windows, database DDL executions, or sudden downstream degradation, developers have no managed facade to dynamically pause or resume consumption for specific listener endpoints or consumer groups without taking down the entire application or changing configuration files.
6. **Sample Project Architecture Invariant Violation (Controller Pollution)**:
   Per the repository's core engineering rules, non-web infrastructure starters must have zero controller pollution in their scenario sample modules. `ateng-boot-sample-rocketmq` currently retains an outdated `RocketmqScenarioController.java` and depends on `spring-boot-starter-web`, violating the architectural baseline. In addition, the sample lacks dual-mode (`local` profile vs. offline in-memory test double) configuration templates.

---

## Solution

Harden and expand `ateng-boot-rocketmq` and `ateng-boot-sample-rocketmq` into a 100% production-ready, full-scenario messaging and distributed transaction infrastructure suite anchored on ADR-0039 and ADR-0066:

1. **Symmetrical Dead Letter Governance Facade (`RocketmqDeadLetterReplayTemplate`)**:
   Provide a dedicated facade targeting `%DLQ%<ConsumerGroup>`. Support `peekDeadLetters(group, limit)` for read-only inspection without ACK, and `replayDeadLetters(group, limit, [targetTopic])` for safe re-enqueueing. The replay logic automatically sanitizes underlying RocketMQ retry properties, injects `X-Dead-Letter-Replayed: true` and an incremented `X-Dead-Letter-Replay-Count`, enforces a maximum replay threshold (default 3) to halt secondary avalanches, and commits `ack` on source dead letters only upon confirmed delivery.
2. **Stream Pull & Lease Control Facade (`RocketmqSimpleConsumerTemplate`)**:
   Introduce a high-level facade based on RocketMQ 5.x `SimpleConsumer`. Expose explicit primitives `receive(topic, group, maxCount, invisibleDuration)`, `ack(messageView)`, and `changeInvisibleDuration(messageView, duration)`. Provide a higher-order closure `receiveAndExecute(...)` that encapsulates type-inferred deserialization, 4D context restoration (MDC/Tenant/User), lease management, and automatic ACK upon success. Manage physical `SimpleConsumer` clients via lazy thread-safe caching in `ConcurrentHashMap` with clean disposal on container shutdown.
3. **Scheduled Message Precision Recall (`RocketmqTemplate.recallMessage`)**:
   Expose `recallMessage(topic, recallHandle)` and `recallMessageAsync(topic, recallHandle)` in `RocketmqTemplate`. Leverage native RocketMQ 5.x `Producer.recallMessage`, returning `RecallReceipt` and translating expired or already-consumed errors into clear business exceptions.
4. **Batch & Oneway Transmission Facades (`RocketmqTemplate`)**:
   Add `sendBatch(topic, [tag], payloads, [timeout])` and `sendBatchAsync(...)` with a hard limit of 500 messages per batch to prevent OOM. Concurrently dispatch via managed async executor and aggregate receipts via `CompletableFuture.allOf`. Add `sendOneway(topic, [tag], [bizKey], payload)` for non-blocking fire-and-forget telemetry.
5. **Runtime Consumer Flow Control Facade (`RocketmqContainerManager`)**:
   Provide an operations facade managing all active `@RocketmqListener` endpoints. Expose `getEndpoints()`, `getEndpoint(id)`, `pause(id)`, `resume(id)`, `stop(id)`, `start(id)`, `isPaused(id)`, and `isRunning(id)`. When paused, incoming messages immediately return `ConsumeResult.FAILURE` to leverage broker-side stepped backoff without memory or thread starvation.
6. **Sample Project Decoupling & Dual-Mode Alignment**:
   Completely remove `spring-boot-starter-web` and `RocketmqScenarioController` from `ateng-boot-sample-rocketmq`. Restructure scenarios into pure `ScenarioService` components. Restrict `InMemoryRocketmqBroker` to `@Profile("!local")` and provide `application-local.example.yml` with optional configuration import for zero-risk real-broker validation.

---

## User Stories

1. As a trade system developer, I want to send a batch of reconciliation messages via `RocketmqTemplate.sendBatch`, so that I can achieve high transmission throughput without writing manual dispatch loops.
2. As a platform architect, I want `sendBatch` to enforce a hard upper bound of 500 messages per call, so that rogue business loops cannot trigger out-of-memory errors or flood broker gRPC buffers.
3. As a telemetry engineer, I want to dispatch audit events and access pings via `RocketmqTemplate.sendOneway`, so that the caller thread is never blocked waiting for network round-trips.
4. As an e-commerce order engineer, I want to recall a delayed auto-cancellation message using its `recallHandle` when a user pays early, so that downstream services avoid unnecessary database state checks.
5. As a developer recalling a delayed message, I want clear semantic exceptions if the recall handle has already expired, so that my domain service can gracefully handle race conditions.
6. As a batch ETL developer, I want to pull messages on-demand using `RocketmqSimpleConsumerTemplate.receive`, so that I can process records in controlled micro-batches instead of being overwhelmed by push streams.
7. As a long-running task developer, I want to extend a message's invisible lease duration via `changeInvisibleDuration`, so that the broker does not re-deliver the message to other workers while my job is still executing.
8. As a consumer developer, I want to process messages via `receiveAndExecute` with automatic type inference and context restoration, so that I do not have to write boilerplate deserialization and ACK code.
9. As a cloud-native developer, I want `RocketmqSimpleConsumerTemplate` to pool and reuse physical `SimpleConsumer` instances per consumer group, so that my service does not open excessive gRPC connections.
10. As an SRE operator, I want to query all registered RocketMQ listener endpoints and their running statuses via `RocketmqContainerManager.getEndpoints`, so that I have full operational visibility into active consumers.
11. As an operations engineer, I want to dynamically pause consumption for a specific consumer group during downstream maintenance via `pause(id)`, so that messages naturally buffer in the broker without crashing downstream databases.
12. As a consumer container, I want paused endpoints to return `ConsumeResult.FAILURE` to the broker, so that message retry intervals provide natural stepped backoff without blocking consumer thread pools.
13. As an operations engineer, I want to resume paused consumption via `resume(id)`, so that consumers immediately resume normal processing without restarting the microservice.
14. As an SRE, I want to inspect dead letters in `%DLQ%<ConsumerGroup>` without acknowledging them via `RocketmqDeadLetterReplayTemplate.peekDeadLetters`, so that I can diagnose the root cause of consumption failures.
15. As a maintenance engineer, I want to safely replay messages from a dead letter queue back to the original topic via `replayDeadLetters`, so that fixed business transactions are processed without manual data compensation.
16. As a governance architect, I want replayed dead letters to have their internal retry properties sanitized, so that consumer frameworks treat them as fresh messages instead of instantly failing them.
17. As an SRE, I want replayed messages to carry `X-Dead-Letter-Replay-Count` and be halted if they exceed 3 replays, so that recurring unresolvable bugs cannot trigger infinite dead-letter recycling storms.
18. As a compliance engineer, I want dead letter messages to be acknowledged and removed from the DLQ only after successful re-delivery, so that no messages are lost if network errors occur during replay.
19. As a framework developer, I want `ateng-boot-sample-rocketmq` to have zero Web Controller dependencies and demonstrate features solely via `ScenarioService`, so that the sample complies with repository-wide architectural invariants.
20. As a CI engineer, I want the RocketMQ test suite to run hermetically in memory by default under `@Profile("!local")` while supporting real-broker integration when `local` is active, so that CI pipelines build in seconds without external network dependencies.

---

## Implementation Decisions

### Modules Modified
- `ateng-boot-rocketmq`: core infrastructure starter.
- `ateng-boot-samples/ateng-boot-sample-rocketmq`: 1:1 scenario integration sample.

### Facades & Contracts Added
- **`RocketmqTemplate` Extensions**:
  - `sendBatch(String topic, [String tag], List<?> payloads, [Duration timeout])`: Concurrent pipeline dispatch with `CompletableFuture.allOf` aggregation. Enforces `payloads != null && !payloads.isEmpty()` and `payloads.size() <= 500`.
  - `sendBatchAsync(String topic, [String tag], List<?> payloads)`: Returns `CompletableFuture<List<SendReceipt>>`.
  - `sendOneway(String topic, [String tag], [String bizKey], Object payload, [Map<String, String> userProperties])`: Fire-and-forget dispatch.
  - `recallMessage(String topic, String recallHandle)`: Direct invocation of native 5.x `Producer.recallMessage`.
  - `recallMessageAsync(String topic, String recallHandle)`: Returns `CompletableFuture<RecallReceipt>`.
- **`RocketmqSimpleConsumerTemplate`**:
  - `receive(String topic, String consumerGroup, int maxMessageNum, Duration invisibleDuration) -> List<MessageView>`.
  - `ack(MessageView messageView)` / `ackAsync(...)`.
  - `changeInvisibleDuration(MessageView messageView, Duration invisibleDuration)` / `changeInvisibleDurationAsync(...)`.
  - `receiveAndExecute(String topic, String consumerGroup, int maxMessageNum, Duration invisibleDuration, Class<T> targetType, Consumer<T> consumer)`.
  - Internal thread-safe cache `ConcurrentHashMap<String, SimpleConsumer>` managed via `PushConsumerFactory` (or companion `SimpleConsumerFactory`) and closed in `destroy()`.
- **`RocketmqContainerManager`**:
  - Methods: `getEndpointIds()`, `getEndpoints()`, `getEndpoint(String id)`, `pause(String id)`, `resume(String id)`, `stop(String id)`, `start(String id)`, `isPaused(String id)`, `isRunning(String id)`.
  - Interacts with `RocketmqConsumerContainer` and sets `volatile boolean paused` in `RocketmqListenerInvoker`.
- **`RocketmqDeadLetterReplayTemplate`**:
  - Automatically targets topic `%DLQ%<consumerGroup>`.
  - Methods: `peekDeadLetters(String consumerGroup, int maxCount) -> List<MessageView>`, `replayDeadLetters(String consumerGroup, int maxCount, [String targetTopic]) -> int`.
  - Strips internal retry headers, injects `X-Dead-Letter-Replayed: true`, `X-Replay-Time`, and incremented `X-Dead-Letter-Replay-Count`.
  - Fails fast / blocks if replay count exceeds max threshold (default 3).
  - ACKs source message upon successful replay.
- **`AtengRocketmqProperties` Configuration Expansion**:
  - `producer.max-batch-size`: integer (default 500).
  - `simple-consumer.invisible-duration`: Duration (default 30s).
  - `simple-consumer.max-message-num`: integer (default 32).
  - `dead-letter.max-replay-attempts`: integer (default 3).
  - `dead-letter.default-batch-size`: integer (default 100).
- **AutoConfiguration Wiring**:
  - Register `RocketmqSimpleConsumerTemplate`, `RocketmqContainerManager`, and `RocketmqDeadLetterReplayTemplate` as `@Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean` in `AtengRocketmqAutoConfiguration`.

### Sample Engineering Cleanup
- Remove `spring-boot-starter-web` and `RocketmqScenarioController.java`.
- Create scenario services: `StandardRocketmqScenarioService`, `TransactionOrderScenarioService`, `BatchDelayScenarioService`, `SimpleConsumerPullScenarioService`, `DeadLetterReplayScenarioService`, and `ContainerOpsScenarioService`.
- Configure `InMemoryRocketmqBroker` under `@Profile("!local")`.
- Provide `application-local.example.yml` and `optional:classpath:application-local.yml` in `application.yml`.

---

## Testing Decisions

- **Test Seam Strategy**:
  - **Component / Facade Seam (`ateng-boot-rocketmq`)**: Unit and component tests verify public facades against the in-memory test double `InMemoryRocketmqBroker` and mock provider with zero network overhead:
    - `RocketmqTemplateTest`: batch send bounds, concurrent pipeline aggregation, oneway dispatch, recall message handling.
    - `RocketmqSimpleConsumerTemplateTest`: pull, manual ack, lease renewal (`changeInvisibleDuration`), functional closure `receiveAndExecute`.
    - `RocketmqContainerManagerTest`: pause/resume state toggling, failure return when paused, stop/start lifecycle.
    - `RocketmqDeadLetterReplayTemplateTest`: peek without ack, safe replay, header sanitization, replay count avalanche defense.
  - **End-to-End Integration Seam (`ateng-boot-sample-rocketmq`)**: `SampleRocketmqE2eTest` runs under `@SpringBootTest` directly invoking `*ScenarioService` beans, asserting end-to-end event delivery, 2PC transaction recovery, simple consumer lease pulling, container pausing, and dead letter replay without any HTTP/Controller layer.
- **Dual-Mode Requirement**:
  - Default/CI mode: 100% hermetic and offline, executing all scenarios in memory within seconds.
  - Local mode: Activating `local` profile bypasses the in-memory double and directly exercises against a real RocketMQ 5.x broker/proxy.
- **Prior Art**: Follow the patterns established in `ateng-boot-rabbitmq` (`RabbitDeadLetterReplayTemplateTest`, `SampleRabbitmqE2eTest`) and `ateng-boot-kafka` (`KafkaDeadLetterReplayTemplateTest`, `KafkaContainerManagerTest`, `SampleKafkaE2eTest`).

---

## Out of Scope

- Integrating legacy 4.x Remoting protocol or `rocketmq-tools` admin client (strictly adheres to the lean Shaded gRPC 5.2.2 baseline).
- Multi-cluster cross-region replication routing.
- Custom Schema Registry serialization (standard JSON + Jackson type inference foundation maintained).

---

## Further Notes

- Fully aligned with [ADR-0039](docs/adr/0039-rocketmq-grpc-and-native-transaction-architecture.md) and [ADR-0066](docs/adr/0066-rocketmq-full-scenario-hardening-simple-consumer-and-dead-letter-governance-architecture.md).
- Preserves 100% backward compatibility for all existing public APIs, annotations (`@RocketmqListener`), and properties (`ateng.boot.rocketmq.*`).

items.body:
## Summary

Add a new **Vector Databases & RAG** documentation section at **Guides & References / Databases**
(`modules/ROOT/pages/database/vector-rag/`). It is a **practical, vendor-neutral guide to using vector
databases as the retrieval layer of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems driven by AI agents**.

The section contains:

* a landing page with a **Bibliography**
* **one detailed page per concept** explored in the requester-provided book and in the official documentation
* a one-page downloadable **cheat sheet PDF**

Each concept page has:

* detailed explanations
* code examples, each linked to the official documentation it derives from
* Mermaid/SVG figures where they help

The section fills the gap between two kinds of existing content:

* the **engine-specific** vector pages that already exist (Qdrant, Redis, Elasticsearch, Solr, Lucene, Neo4j, MongoDB, Couchbase)
* the **LangChain** and **Spring AI** documentation sections that will be added by future issues

It explains the concepts every engine shares:

* embeddings
* similarity metrics and semantic search
* ANN indexes and quantization
* metadata filtering, hybrid search and re-ranking
* the SQL-extension route (SQLite and PostgreSQL/pgvector)
* a **comparison of the vector databases** mentioned in this section and elsewhere on the site (Qdrant, PostgreSQL/pgvector, Redis, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, MongoDB, Neo4j, Couchbase, Solr/Lucene, Milvus, Weaviate, Pinecone, Chroma, LanceDB, SQLite, and the AWS / Google Cloud / Azure native services): strengths and weaknesses in performance, scalability, price and cloud availability
* the RAG pipeline, agentic RAG and agent memory
* evaluation and production concerns

It also shows **how a vector store plugs into AI agents through LangChain (Python, plus LangChain4j for Java) and
Spring AI**. Those integration pages are deliberately scoped so the future LangChain / Spring AI sections can link to them
and extend them rather than duplicate them.

## Context

### Requester-provided book

The PDF is a copyrighted work. It is **not** attached to this issue or uploaded anywhere; its publisher page is linked
instead.

**`~/Desktop/vector.pdf`** is:

* **Title:** **_Vector Databases: A Practical Introduction_**
* **Author and publisher:** **Nitin Borwankar**, **O'Reilly Media, 2026**
* **ISBN:** **978-1-098-17759-1** (print)
* **Length:** 9 chapters, ~290 pages
* **Code:** Python 3.11+, CPU-only, self-hosted
* **Stack:** FAISS, SQLite3 + sqlite-vss, PostgreSQL + pgvector, sentence-transformers `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384 dims), and Ollama `llama3.1:8b`
* **Official code:** https://github.com/nborwankar/VectorDatabaseBook (MIT)

The book is a **consulted reference for the concept narrative, the practitioner's angle and the bibliography**. It
is never the primary source for any code example. Every example is written against the current official
documentation, and on any discrepancy the official documentation wins.

Chapters and the concepts each contributes:

| Ch. | Title | Concepts extracted |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Introduction to Vector Databases | Why unstructured data needs semantic (not keyword) search. The `VECTOR` data type and its operations (similarity comparison, nearest-neighbour/ANN, vector arithmetic). Use cases. SQL vs. vector databases (`FLOAT[]` in an RDBMS and its limits). NoSQL vector extensions (Redis, MongoDB Atlas, Elasticsearch, Cassandra), their limits, and when they are enough. **Hybrid architecture**: vector component + metadata component + integration layer, and a hybrid query combining similarity, metadata filters and sorting. |
| 2 | Embeddings | Embedding as verb and as noun. Word2Vec and the King − Man + Woman ≈ Queen arithmetic. Doc2Vec. Transformer embeddings (encoder-only BERT, decoder-only GPT, encoder-decoder T5/BART). **Dedicated embedding models** and contrastive learning. The embedding model's role in the RAG pattern. sentence-transformers best practices (batching, max sequence length and chunking, **normalization**, GPU/MPS, memory management, error handling). Multilingual models. The embedding layer and zero-shot classification. CLIP cross-modal embeddings. Limitations (domain vocabulary, dimensionality cost). |
| 3 | Similarity Search with FAISS | Distance metrics (L2 / squared L2, inner product, cosine) and selection heuristics. FAISS index families: Flat, IVF (`nlist`, `nprobe`, training), LSH, HNSW (`M`, `efConstruction`, `efSearch`, memory rule of thumb), binary indexes, composite indexes (`IndexPreTransform`/PCA, `IndexIDMap`, `IndexRefineFlat`, `IndexShards`), and `index_factory` strings. The index-selection decision tree and the index properties table (bytes/vector). **Quantization**: SQ (codebooks, SQ8/SQ4/fp16) and **PQ** (subspaces, k-means codebooks, IVFADC/IVFPQ, refinement). The ANN problem and the (1+ε) approximation. FAISS architecture. |
| 4 | Semantic Search with SQLite3 | The sqlite-vss extension (`vector0` + `vss0` virtual table wrapping FAISS). The **two-table pattern** (content table + vector virtual table joined by `rowid`). The `INSERT OR REPLACE` rowid pitfall (use UPSERT). Keeping the raw embedding BLOB for re-indexing. Flat vs. `HNSW16`/`IVF…` factory strings. Rebuild vs. incremental indexing. **"Overfetch-then-filter"** because metadata predicates are not pushed down into the ANN search. Distance-to-score conversion. The text cleaning and quality-filtering pipeline and batch embedding pipeline. |
| 5 | ArXiv Paper Search with PostgreSQL pgvector | Architecture and data flow of a search system. Schema design: papers, chunks, a processing queue, and `vector(384)` columns. **HNSW index parameters** (`m = 16`, `ef_construction = 64`, recall > 0.95). B-tree, GIN and trigram indexes for metadata. Chunk size (512–1,024 tokens, 20% overlap, sentence boundaries, section context). PDF extraction challenges. Batch embedding. Docker Compose packaging. Basic performance tuning. |
| 6 | RAG System with SQLite VSS and Ollama | The end-to-end local RAG architecture and a schema for RAG (posts + chunks + VSS + **FTS5**). Word-window chunking with overlap. **Hybrid search**: semantic plus BM25 keyword search, and score normalization (BM25 is unbounded; cosine is bounded). Weighted fusion (0.7 / 0.3) and score dominance. The Ollama client (low temperature, the silent `num_ctx` 2,048 truncation). Context formatting with source attribution and popularity bias. The QA pipeline with timings. Production considerations (incremental updates, deletion orphans, embedding cache, pooling, batching). Advanced patterns: multi-hop, source diversity, confidence scoring, fact verification. |
| 7 | Scientific RAG with PostgreSQL and pgvector | HNSW with `vector_cosine_ops`, and dropping or recreating the index for bulk loads. **Multilevel semantic search**: abstract-level plus section-level search, merged and sorted. The `<=>` cosine distance, `1 − distance` similarity, and **similarity thresholds** (0.8 / 0.7 / 0.6). Retrieval vs. display thresholds. **Lost in the middle / primacy bias** and context assembly within the context window. Domain prompt engineering. A **technical note on HNSW complexity**: O(log n) is a heuristic, not a theorem, and where query cost lands depends on `efSearch`, `M`, intrinsic dimension and the recall target. **Evaluation**: retrieval depth/recall, context relevance, faithfulness, RAGAS, LLM-as-a-judge, IR metrics. Next steps: re-ranking with cross-encoders, knowledge-graph concept linking, and incremental updates. |
| 8 | Conversation Search and RAG System | Conversational data (contextual dependencies, privacy). A three-table schema that separates the `message_embeddings` table so the model can be changed. HNSW indexing. Atomic imports. Singleton model loading, incremental embedding and batch processing with conflict handling. **Context-window retrieval around a hit** (±N messages). A RAG pipeline over personal chat history, i.e. **agent / assistant memory**. A FastAPI search and RAG API. |
| 9 | Vector Query Language | The fragmentation of vector DB APIs and a proposed SQL-like **VQL**. Data model: collection, table, vector, embedding, field, metadata and distance metric. `SIMILARITY SEARCH … USING METRIC … TOP K`, filtered and thresholded search, `HYBRID SEARCH` with weights, `RANGE SEARCH`, and batch search. Vector functions and aggregations (`DIMENSION`, `DISTANCE`, `DOT`, arithmetic, centroid `AVG`, `GEOMETRIC_MEDIAN`). This is a speculative proposal, not a standard. |

### Where the book is outdated or narrower than the official docs

When a page draws on the book, it must say where the book is outdated or narrower and document the current approach:

* **sqlite-vss is deprecated.** Its last release was v0.1.2 (2023) and its README says it is not in active development. The current successor is
  **sqlite-vec 0.1.9** (`vec0` virtual tables, `MATCH` KNN queries, and metadata / partition-key columns that remove much of the
  overfetch-then-filter need). The SQLite page documents sqlite-vec. The sqlite-vss architecture is mentioned only as history,
  as the conceptual precursor of "FAISS inside a relational DB".
* **pgvector has moved beyond the book.** The book uses only `vector` + HNSW with `vector_cosine_ops`. Current **pgvector 0.8.6** also has:
  * the `halfvec`, `sparsevec` and `bit` types
  * the `<+>` (L1), `<~>` (Hamming) and `<%>` (Jaccard) operators
  * IVFFlat
  * **iterative index scans** (`hnsw.iterative_scan`), which fix the filtered-search under-return problem
  * binary quantization via expression indexes
* **Weighted linear score fusion is only one option.** The book's 0.7 / 0.3 weighted fusion must be contrasted with **Reciprocal Rank Fusion**, which is what most engines and
  frameworks now implement: Qdrant, Elasticsearch retrievers, Redis `FT.HYBRID`, Spring AI / LangChain ensemble retrievers.
* **The RAG code is hand-rolled.** The book builds RAG by hand in Python. The official documentation of **LangChain 1.x / LangGraph 1.x**,
  **LangChain4j 1.20** and **Spring AI 2.0** provides the same building blocks as framework abstractions, and the
  integration pages must use them: loaders, splitters, `VectorStore`, retrievers, advisors, agents and tools.
* **Agentic RAG is only sketched.** The book mentions multi-hop and iterative retrieval only as future work. Agentic RAG (retriever-as-tool,
  routing, self-correction), MCP-exposed retrieval and agent memory are documented from the official LangChain / LangGraph /
  Spring AI / MCP docs.
* **Some concepts are missing from the book.** The docs and papers must supply:
  * Matryoshka / truncatable embeddings
  * late chunking and contextual retrieval
  * sparse vectors (SPLADE / BM25 as sparse)
  * cross-encoder re-ranking as a first-class step
  * DiskANN / Vamana and binary quantization with rescoring
  * GraphRAG
  * semantic caching
  * managed vector services

### What already exists in this repository

Do **not** re-document these pages. Link to them and add only what they do not cover.

| Existing page | What it already covers | Relationship to the new section |
|---|---|---|
| `database/choosing-the-right-database.adoc` → `== Vector Databases` / `=== Choosing one` | A short vendor list (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate/Qdrant, Milvus, and reuse of ES/Solr/Couchbase/MongoDB/Redis), with a "Vector → pgvector / Qdrant / Milvus" decision leaf | Gains a pointer to the new landing page and to the landscape and comparison pages. The new comparison page is the in-depth, evaluated version of that list. |
| `database/qdrant/*`, especially `vector-indexing-and-hnsw.adoc`, `hybrid-and-sparse-search.adoc` and `rag-integration-patterns.adoc` (which includes a `langchain-qdrant` section) | Qdrant-specific HNSW, quantization, sparse vectors + RRF, and RAG with Qdrant | Linked as the **purpose-built engine** worked example. The generic ANN, quantization, hybrid and RAG pages explain the concepts once and point here for the Qdrant realisation. The Qdrant RAG page gains a link back to the generic RAG pages. |
| `database/redis/vector-search.adoc`, `database/redis/spring-boot-redis-as-a-vector-database.adoc` (Spring AI 2.0 `RedisVectorStore`, `QuestionAnswerAdvisor`, chat memory), `database/redis/use-cases-and-patterns.adoc` (semantic cache and agent memory) | Redis-specific vector search and Spring AI with Redis | The Spring AI integration page is **store-agnostic** (it uses pgvector as its default) and links here for the Redis variant; nothing is repeated. The semantic-cache and agent-memory material is linked from the agent memory page. |
| `database/elasticsearch/vector-and-semantic-search.adoc`, `database/solr/dense-vector-search.adoc`, `database/lucene/knn-vector-search.adoc`, `database/neo4j/vector-search-and-genai.adoc` (GraphRAG), `database/mongodb/special-indexes-and-search.adoc` (Atlas Vector Search), `database/couchbase/search-analytics-eventing.adoc` (vector + hybrid) | Engine-specific kNN, HNSW, hybrid and semantic features | Referenced from the landscape and comparison pages and from the concept pages as "how engine X does it". Each gains one sentence linking back to the relevant concept page. |
| `database/neo4j/similarity-embeddings-and-ml-pipelines.adoc` | *Graph* embeddings (FastRP, Node2Vec, GraphSAGE) | The embeddings page distinguishes text/multimodal embeddings from graph embeddings and links here. |
| `backend/springboot/index.adoc`, `backend/springboot/solr.adoc`, `backend/springboot/spring-data-neo4j.adoc`, `backend/springboot/spring-data-couchbase.adoc` (vector search) | Spring integrations per store | The Spring Boot index gains a bullet pointing at the Spring AI integration page of the new section. |
| `backend/quarkus/extensions-and-the-platform.adoc` (a one-line mention of Quarkiverse LangChain4j) | none | Can link the LangChain page's LangChain4j subsection. |
| `apps/apple/apple-intelligence-and-machine-learning.adoc` | On-device models, tool calling and prompt injection | Linked from the production/security page's prompt-injection discussion. |

**No page in the repository explains the concepts themselves, across engines.** Missing today:

* embeddings, and how to choose, normalize, version and migrate them
* similarity metrics and the distance vs. similarity conversion
* the ANN problem
* IVF, LSH, HNSW complexity and PQ theory
* FAISS
* SQLite (sqlite-vec) and PostgreSQL (pgvector) as vector databases
* metadata filtering strategies (pre-, post- and iterative filtering)
* score fusion theory
* chunking strategies
* the RAG pipeline end to end
* retrieval strategies (multilevel, parent/context expansion, query transformation, MMR)
* agentic RAG and agent memory
* RAG evaluation
* production and security concerns
* a vector/RAG cheat sheet

### Future LangChain and Spring AI sections: integration contract

Separate issues will later add full **LangChain** and **Spring AI** documentation sections. To keep the three sections
coherent:

* **Scope of this section.** The two integration pages (`integrating-with-langchain.adoc`, `integrating-with-spring-ai.adoc`)
  document **only the vector-store / retrieval / RAG / agent-memory surface** of each framework:
  * embeddings
  * document loading and splitting
  * vector store APIs
  * retrievers
  * RAG advisors and chains
  * retriever-as-tool in agents
  * vector-backed chat memory

  Out of scope, and reserved for the future sections: chat model configuration in depth, prompt templates, structured output,
  general tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, LangSmith, Spring AI observability, and the MCP server/client APIs beyond the
  retrieval use case.
* **No dangling cross-references.** Antora fails on unresolved `xref:`s, so these pages link to the frameworks' **official** documentation. They must **not** `xref:` pages that
  don't exist yet.
* **Stable anchors.** Every integration page uses explicit, stable section IDs (for example `[[langchain-vector-stores]]`,
  `[[langchain-agentic-rag]]`, `[[spring-ai-vector-store-api]]`, `[[spring-ai-rag-advisors]]`,
  `[[spring-ai-chat-memory]]`). The future sections can then deep-link into them and eventually replace an anchor's
  body with a pointer.
* **Portable abstractions as a principle.** Each concept page ends with a short "In LangChain / In Spring AI" subsection showing the framework
  abstraction for that concept (e.g. filtering → Spring AI `FilterExpressionBuilder` / LangChain `filter=`). The
  integration story is therefore visible at every step, not only on the two integration pages. The landscape page
  explicitly positions `VectorStore` (LangChain, Spring AI) and `EmbeddingStore` (LangChain4j) as today's de facto answer to
  the portability problem the book's Chapter 9 VQL proposal addresses.
* **Future pointers go in plain prose.** Each integration page's intro states, in plain prose, that a complete LangChain / Spring AI section is
  planned and that this page covers only the vector-database side. This is not an admonition: see the admonition rule below.

## New nav placement

```
Guides & References
└─ Databases                              modules/ROOT/pages/database/index.adoc              (add a bullet)
   ├─ … SQL / MongoDB / … / Qdrant / Redis Reference                                          (unchanged)
   ├─ Vector Databases & RAG             modules/ROOT/pages/database/vector-rag/index.adoc
   │  └─ (23 concept pages + cheat sheet, listed below)
```

items.body:
## Context

The single biggest CRITICAL gap the CTO Master review flagged in ActOne XSE: **the tenancy model is invisible**. Pooled-RDS vs silo-RDS vs cell-based is not knowable from the diagram. Without it, none of these questions are answerable:

- Can a noisy tenant break a quiet one?
- Can BYOK be offered per tenant?
- Can a tenant be exported within GDPR DSAR's 30-day SLA?
- What is the blast radius of an incident?

This is an **executive-grade gap** that downstream blocks 6+ other decisions. A human reviewer flagged it. Archmorph did not — because it has no concept of tenancy.

This is a **new orthogonal capability**, not a single rule.

## What it should detect

Inspect the architecture for tenancy signals:

| Tenancy model | Signals |
|---|---|
| **Silo** (one stack per tenant) | Per-customer VPC / project / subscription / RDS instance; tenant-id in resource names |
| **Pooled** (shared everything) | Single RDS, single Kafka, tenant-id in row keys / table partition / topic header |
| **Cell-based** | Multiple identical "cells" with tenants pinned per cell; cell-aware routing |
| **Hybrid** | Pooled compute + silo data, or vice versa |
| **Unknown** (default) | None of the above clearly identifiable |

Output a `TenancyModel` classification with confidence and the signals supporting it. Add a dedicated **"Tenancy" section** to the analysis output covering:

1. Detected model
2. Blast-radius estimate (% of tenants impacted by a single-resource failure)
3. BYOK feasibility (yes / partial / no)
4. GDPR-DSAR feasibility (≤ 30 days y/n)
5. Noisy-neighbour risk score
6. Recommended next step

## Output

```
[HIGH] Tenancy model not determinable — executive decision required
  Detected: UNKNOWN (no clear silo / pool / cell signals)
  Implications:
    - Blast-radius: unbounded (worst case: 100% of tenants on one shared RDS)
    - BYOK feasibility: NO (cannot offer per-tenant CMK without silo or cell)
    - GDPR-DSAR ≤ 30d: AT RISK (export in pooled requires schema-aware ETL)
    - Noisy-neighbour risk: HIGH
  CTO action:
    - Document current state in 30 days.
    - Choose target model (recommend cell-based for tier-1 customers).
    - Tag every resource with `tenant-id`.
    - Cell-based migration roadmap on 24-month horizon.
  Why CTO-owned:
    - Tenancy choice is a multi-year, multi-million-dollar architectural commitment.
    - It is not an SRE / ops decision.
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New module `backend/architecture_review/tenancy_detector.py`
- [ ] `TenancyModel` enum + `TenancyClassification` dataclass with confidence + supporting signals
- [ ] Outputs a dedicated "Tenancy" section in the analysis (visible in Architecture Health panel and IaC chat replies)
- [ ] Five-question scorecard (blast radius, BYOK, DSAR, noisy-neighbour, recommendation)
- [ ] Test fixture: ActOne XSE diagram → returns `UNKNOWN`, emits HIGH finding
- [ ] Test fixture: mocked silo / pool / cell architectures → correct classification each

### What happened/what did you expect to happen?

We have set our Argo Workflows with `parallelism: 2048` and `- --qps=2048`. We have no `namespaceParallelism`. We are also running 5 Workflow Controllers. The system runs up to 3000 workflows during the day in 2 different namespaces. However, we have noticed that we end up having a lot of Pending workflows with the message: `Workflow processing has been postponed because too many workflows are already running` while there are 0 `Running` workflows at that very moment, and 2000+ workflows marked as `Succeeded`. Our default TTL for workflows is 24h but we did add some in the last week that have a longer TTL - 3-4 days for some jobs.

The moment I manually delete all the `Succeeded` workflows using `kubectl delete wf -n argo -l workflows.argoproj.io/phase=Succeeded` the workflows get unclogged and everything runs as normal. While it is not a problem to lower the TTL for successful jobs I am wondering if this is intended behaviour or if we are missing something in our configuration. I have read the whole default `values.yaml` in the Helm chart for Argo Worfklows but I didn't see anything pointing to this particular issue.
